Disclaimers, intended use, and how your data is handled

Odd Health and the readings it shows are for general wellness and personal interest only. They are not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, monitor or prevent any disease or condition, and must not replace advice from a qualified health professional. If you feel unwell or are worried about your health, contact a doctor. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
Viewing the data your own Even Realities R1 ring records, keeping a copy on your phone, and sharing it with Health Connect so other wellness apps you choose can use it.

• Medical decisions, including starting, stopping or changing any treatment or medication
• Monitoring anyone's health without their knowledge or consent
• Detecting or alerting on emergencies: the app does not raise alarms, and data can arrive hours late
• Clinical, research or legal evidence
• Monitoring of infants, or of anyone whose safety depends on it

The ring reports heart rate, HRV and blood oxygen as hourly averages, so short changes don\'t show. Resting heart rate is an estimate made by this app from those averages, and reads higher than a true resting rate. Temperature is measured at the finger and reads about 1 °C below core temperature. Sleep stages and the sleep score come from the ring\'s own algorithms. This app reads the ring through an unofficial, reverse-engineered protocol: a ring firmware update can change what it sends, and values can be wrong or missing without warning.

Everything stays on this phone. Odd Health has no account, no servers, no analytics and no ads. Its only internet use is checking GitHub for app updates and downloading them, which sends no health data. Data is stored in the app\'s private storage and excluded from cloud backups and device transfers, so uninstalling the app deletes it.\n\nData only leaves the app when you choose to: by writing it to Health Connect, or by sharing debug logs (off by default), which contain health data and your ring\'s Bluetooth address.

With your permission, Odd Health writes heart rate, resting heart rate, HRV, blood oxygen, steps, calories, sleep and temperature to Health Connect. It does not read any data from Health Connect. Once written, other apps you allow can read it under their own privacy policies. You can change permissions or delete Odd Health\'s data in Health Connect settings at any time.
Your ring and the Even app

Odd Health shares the ring\'s Bluetooth connection with the Even app and only reads data. It never marks data as synced on the ring, never changes ring settings or firmware, and never touches the ring\'s pairing with your glasses. Keep the Even app installed for firmware updates and pairing.
Odd Health is an independent open-source project. It is not made, endorsed or supported by Even Realities, Google or any device or health-platform maker. Product names belong to their owners.

Odd Health is not a medical device. The readings are for general wellness and personal interest only, may be inaccurate or delayed, and must not be used for medical decisions or emergencies.\n\nYour data stays on this phone unless you choose to write it to Health Connect or share debug logs.
Check for a new version on GitHub
This is a test build. Updates from GitHub are signed with a different key, so install the release from GitHub after uninstalling this build.
Checks GitHub once a day and shows a notification when a new version is out

Update checks contact GitHub (api.github.com and github.com) to read the latest release and download it. Nothing else is sent: no health data and no identifiers. GitHub sees your IP address, as with any web request. Downloads are checked against the release\'s checksum, and Android only installs updates signed with the same key as the installed app.
Open an issue on GitHub, optionally with a debug log

This opens the project\'s bug report form on GitHub in your browser, with the app version, Android version, phone model and ring firmware filled in. You can edit or remove any of them before submitting. You need a GitHub account to submit.
Saves the debug logs to your Downloads folder so you can attach them to the issue
No debug logs saved. Turn on debug logging, reproduce the problem, then come back.
Off: turn it on to capture a log

GitHub issues are public. Debug logs contain your health data and your ring\'s Bluetooth address. Only attach the log if you\'re comfortable with that; otherwise mention in the issue that you have one.
Nothing is sent until you submit the form on GitHub. The log file stays in Downloads until you delete it.
